evals.name: refresh-needed
evals.prompt: My `proof-engine@acme-marketplace` plugin in Claude Desktop keeps loading the old 0.3.1 even though I know 0.4.0 is out. I ran `claude plugin update proof-engine@acme-marketplace` but it said 'already at latest version'. I went ahead and ran `cpd --json --no-progress --no-log-file` — its output is in `cpd-output.json`. Diagnose the problem and tell me the exact commands to fix it.
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the marketplace clone is stale (refresh-needed); recommends `claude plugin marketplace update acme-marketplace && claude plugin update proof-engine@acme-marketplace`; presents the fix in plain English without dumping raw JSON; classifies the action as safe and offers to run it.

assertions.name: names refresh-needed or marketplace-clone-stale
assertions.description: Output identifies the underlying drift kind (either by name or by plain-English description: marketplace clone is behind remote).

assertions.name: recommends marketplace-update + plugin-update chain
assertions.description: Output proposes both commands: `claude plugin marketplace update acme-marketplace` and `claude plugin update proof-engine@acme-marketplace`, in that order.

assertions.name: presents fix in plain English
assertions.description: Output translates the JSON into natural language for the user. It does not present the recommendation as a raw JSON paste.

assertions.name: no spurious destructive-warning
assertions.description: The action is safe; the response does not warn about destructive consequences or ask for explicit yes confirmation as if it were destructive.

assertions.name: no false-positive on other drift kinds
assertions.description: Does not invent or attribute the failure to bump-needed, badge-only-needed, or marketplace-update-broken — the actual cause is refresh-needed.

evals.name: force-fetch
evals.prompt: I've been running `claude plugin marketplace update founder-skills` for over a week and it always succeeds, but my plugin still loads the old version (0.2.0). Github's clearly at a newer commit. I ran `cpd --json --no-progress --no-log-file` and its output is in `cpd-output.json`. Walk me through what's happening and what to do.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the marketplace-update-broken trap (Anthropic issue #46081 — silent cooldown). Recommends `cpd refresh founder-skills --force-fetch --yes` as the bypass. Surfaces that this is a destructive operation that writes to .git/ (after backing up), and asks the user to confirm before running. Mentions the underlying cause: the standard `claude plugin marketplace update` is silently failing.

assertions.name: identifies the silent-cooldown / #46081 root cause
assertions.description: Output explicitly identifies that the standard refresh is silently failing (HTTP 304/429/cooldown variant of Anthropic issue #46081 — naming the issue or the silent-failure mechanism counts).

assertions.name: recommends cpd refresh --force-fetch --yes
assertions.description: Output proposes `cpd refresh founder-skills --force-fetch --yes` (or equivalent — the marketplace name, --force-fetch, and --yes are all required for the recommendation to be actionable).

assertions.name: surfaces destructive nature and asks for confirmation
assertions.description: The response flags that --force-fetch writes to .git/ (or otherwise treats this as a destructive/manual-confirmation step), and asks the user to confirm BEFORE running rather than just running it.

assertions.name: mentions backup behavior
assertions.description: Output reassures the user that --force-fetch backs up .git/HEAD and the origin ref before resetting (the safety property that justifies the destructive op).

assertions.name: presents fix in plain English
assertions.description: Output translates the JSON into natural language. Does not present the diagnosis as a raw JSON paste.

evals.name: bump-needed
evals.prompt: I'm a plugin author. I've been editing my plugin's source and pushing commits to the marketplace repo. But `claude plugin update my-dev-plugin@local-mp` keeps saying 'already at latest version' even though I just pushed new code. I ran `cpd --json --no-progress --no-log-file` — output in `cpd-output.json`. What am I doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that `plugin.json#version` was not bumped, so `claude plugin update` is silently a no-op (bump-needed trap). Walks the user through the manual steps: edit plugin.json to bump version, commit, push, then run marketplace update + plugin update. Does NOT try to auto-execute the version bump — explains that this is a manual step the user has to do.

assertions.name: identifies bump-needed / plugin.json#version unchanged
assertions.description: Output explains that `plugin.json#version` did not change across commits, which is why `claude plugin update` is a silent no-op.

assertions.name: presents numbered manual steps
assertions.description: Output walks through the bump process as a numbered or otherwise structured set of manual steps (edit plugin.json, commit, push, update marketplace, update plugin).

assertions.name: does not auto-execute version bump
assertions.description: Output does NOT propose to automatically edit plugin.json or run the bump itself; it leaves the manual step to the user.

assertions.name: presents fix in plain English
assertions.description: Output translates the JSON into natural language for the user, not raw JSON.

assertions.name: no false-positive on refresh-needed
assertions.description: Output does NOT recommend `claude plugin marketplace update` as the standalone fix — that wouldn't help here because the marketplace clone is already fresh; the user has to bump the version first.
